bds.lede: Hundreds of thousands demonstrate over cost of living and cuts to public services as 70,000 police officers deployed
rows: New protests and worker strikes began in France amid cost of living concerns and calls for improved public services. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.
Hundreds of thousands demonstrate over cost of living and cuts to public services as 70,000 police officers deployed

Some protesters clashed with police in Paris and Lyon on Thursday during largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations and a one-day strike by some public sector workers in a renewed challenge to President Emmanuel Macron.

France’s Interior Ministry said more than 600,000 people rallied Thursday across France, including in Paris, to demand higher wages and support the student protest movement, piling fresh pressure on the beleaguered government.
Trade unions led more than 260 planned protests nationwide, urging government to address economic woes and wage demands.
“Everything is going up except wages and pensions,” a statement by the country’s main unions said. “Anger is immense.”
